records.title: Stylo2 Haptics repository (this project)

links.label: Upstream project named in the README

records.summary: The Magisk module and companion app behind the XDA thread. It contains the only working third-party client for the Stylo 2 haptics service found so far.
details: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ holds the reconstructed service interface: ISdkAidlInterface, ISDKAidlCallback, Vibration and IpeFeature. The files are marked as cleaned reconstructions.
OplusPencilSdkClient.kt defines StylusVibrationClient: permission check, bindService, interface-descriptor check, and a StateFlow<Connection> for the UI.
The README says the vibration presets were taken from analysis of the stock OnePlus Notes app.
Build: Kotlin, minSdk 30, targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, AGP 8.13.0, Kotlin 2.0.21.
Known defect: unbind() calls stopVibration() after unbindService(), so the stop command can go to a binder that is already released. Stop first, then unbind.
Known defect: getSupportFeatureList() is declared but has no transaction code and always throws.
records.basis: Read in full from the repository on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: crDroid device tree for caihong: proprietary file list
records.summary: Custom-ROM file list showing how the Pad Pro's pen firmware is laid out: two real directories, each with a second name linked to it.
details: odm/firmware/wireless_pen/23976/cps8601_firmware.bin;SYMLINK=odm/firmware/wireless_pen/23926/cps8601_firmware.bin
odm/firmware/wireless_pen/23978/cps8601_firmware.bin;SYMLINK=odm/firmware/wireless_pen/23927/cps8601_firmware.bin
So a custom ROM covers both directory names with one file each, which is what the community module does by copying.

records.title: oplus-global-pen-enabler (stylus firmware fix module)
records.summary: KernelSU module that restores the Stylo pen after converting a Chinese OnePlus Pad Pro to a global ROM, by adding the missing CPS8601 pen-charger firmware directories.
details: Targets the OnePlus Pad Pro (caihong) and Pad 2 (rainbow) with the Stylo 2 (Chinese name: OnePlus Smart Stylus Pro).

Ships odm/firmware/wireless_pen/{23926,23927,23976,23978,24926}/cps8601_firmware.bin plus module.prop, with no install or boot scripts. Hashes: research/reference/oplus-global-pen-enabler/MANIFEST.md.
The four 239xx files are identical. 24926 is a different build, added on 12 Apr 2026 by contributor FRTI64.
The README explains the method: kernel module info for oplus_wireless_pen.ko, the cps8601 kernel log on attach, and the finding that ROM regions use different firmware directory names.
Swapping the Chinese ROM's odm.img confirmed the cause before the module was written.
Full write-up: research/docs/pen-attach-handshake.md

records.title: fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro (Stylus Fixes for OnePlus, v1.2)
records.summary: The Magisk module from the XDA regional-ROM thread. It copies pen firmware the ROM already has into a directory named after the tablet's own project number, then overlays that onto /odm/firmware.
details: Author jjhitel (Jeong Seongpil). GPL-3.0. v1.0 to v1.2, 4 to 19 Aug 2025. A reference copy of the scripts is in research/reference/fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro/.
Install (customize.sh): reads ro.boot.prjname. Aborts unless it is five digits and ro.product.system.manufacturer is oplus.
Lists the other five-digit directories in /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/, sorted. With one, it uses it. With several, it is meant to take the next untried one on each re-flash, tracked by marker files.
Copies every *.bin from the chosen directory into the module's odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<prjname>/, with SELinux context vendor_configs_file.

Every boot (post-fs-data.sh): mounts an overlay on /odm/firmware with its upper layer in /dev/anyfs (RAM), so the new directory appears alongside the stock ones. It does this mount itself instead of relying on the root manager.
Ships no firmware. It only reuses files already on the tablet.

History: v1.0 supported only the OnePlus Pad 2 Pro (prjname 24926 or 24976). It copied 24976's file into 24926 and forced ro.boot.prjname=24976. v1.1 added the overlay mount (credit AestasBritannia). v1.2 made it generic and stopped forcing the property.

Caveats found in the code: re-flash marker files probably don't survive, because Magisk empties the module folder on each install, so it may always pick the lowest-numbered directory. With no other directory it still reports success. On a tablet that already has its own directory, it replaces that firmware with another variant's.
It doesn't check firmware compatibility, so a successful install doesn't prove the chosen file is right.
Full write-up: research/docs/pen-attach-handshake.md
records.basis: Uploaded v1.2 zip (SHA-256 9371189d…6484331) compared with the GitHub repo at commit 0131a9d; scripts identical. Read 2 Nov 2026.

records.summary: Magisk module thread by jjhitel for the same problem: the stylus stops working after converting between Chinese and global ROMs. The module is fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro.
details: Module behaviour is documented from its code in the fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro record.
Listed for the OnePlus Pad 2 Pro (China) and the Pad 3.
The author says the pen firmware is the same across regions and only the loading path differs, which matches the cxzlw module's finding.

Mixed user reports: one user swapped only odm.img (ColorOS .501 onto OxygenOS .500 EU) and it worked. Another found the KernelSU module did not work and the odm.img swap caused boot crashes. A third says the pen stopped charging after a later global update.
The thread itself could not be read: XDA refuses automated access. User reports here come from search-result excerpts.

records.title: XDA: OnePlus Stylo 2 global haptic feedback
records.summary: Discussion and install thread for the Stylo2 Haptics Magisk module and app, which is the project in this repository.
details: The repository README links this thread for discussion and install instructions.

Module: installs the app to /system/priv-app with a privapp-permissions allowlist on the system, system_ext and product partitions, so Android grants it com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT at boot. The README states that no firmware files are modified.
App: binds to com.oplus.ipemanager with the action com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK and calls setVibrationType and startFeedBackVibration.
Tested only on a OnePlus Pad 3 running Global OxygenOS (converted from OPD2413 ColorOS to OPD2415), Android 16.
records.basis: Repository README checked on 2 Nov 2026. The thread itself was not re-read.

records.title: xiaomi-sheng-thp (Linux userspace pen and touch driver)
records.summary: Userspace driver for the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro 12.4 ("sheng") on Linux. It shows pen position coming from the touch controller and pressure coming over Bluetooth.
details: Reads raw THP frames from the NT36532E touch controller through kernel nodes such as /proc/nvt_thp_stylus and exposes standard input devices through uinput.
Pen coordinates, tilt and hover come from the touch controller stream. Pen scanning works only at 60 Hz or 120 Hz panel refresh.
Pressure comes from the pen's Bluetooth HID reports (BlueZ required).
The Focus Pen Pro posture sensor is read separately through libssc.
No haptics support is mentioned.
C++20, Apache-2.0, runs as root, needs a kernel with the Xiaomi THP nodes.
